neighbours.label: A short two-letter word piece ('ac', 'as', 'us', 'AS') that continues a rare word after a split-off stem: 'em|ac|iated', 'em|as|culated', 'Emma|us', 'AD|AS'; not the same meaning in a word the tokenizer keeps whole or splits differently.
fire: After months in the camp, the prisoners were thin and emaciated.
The vet said the stray cat showed clear signs of emaciation.
Some critics felt the new law emasculated the local councils.
The pilgrims walked the seven miles from Jerusalem to Emmaus.
Most new cars now come with ADAS features such as lane keeping.
The photograph of the emaciated horse shocked the readers.
The reform was meant to emasculate the power of the regional barons.
The painting shows the supper at Emmaus in warm evening light.
quiet: After months in the camp, the prisoners were thin and exhausted.
The vet said the stray cat showed clear signs of hunger.
Some critics felt the new law weakened the local councils.
The pilgrims walked the seven miles from Jerusalem to Bethlehem.
Most new cars now come with safety features such as lane keeping.
The photograph of the starving horse shocked the readers.
The reform was meant to embarrass the regional barons.
The painting shows a green emerald in warm evening light.

short: mid-word piece 'ac'/'as'/'us'/'AS' after a split stem
notes: Probes (fraction of max 11.38): emaciated 'ac' 0.633, Emmaus 'us' 0.861, emasculating 'as' 0.473, ADAS 'AS' 0.668. Other em- words with different splits: emerald 0.011, embalming 0.007, embarrassed (one token) 0.011; synonym 'underfed' 0.008. Splits checked with tok.py: emaciation/emaciated -> em|ac|…, emasculated/emasculate -> em|as|…, Emmaus -> Emma|us, ADAS/CDAS -> AD|AS / CD|AS.
